test.name: Subject-as-child census — assertion-only extraction; flags record-vs-tree children discrepancy
test.description: Converted from ut_record_extraction_013: the record the user pasted is now served as a record_read fixture (the 1850 census household of Thomas Flynn, Schuylkill County, dwelling 84), and extraction runs in code. When the subject (Patrick Flynn) appears as a child in an 1850 census household, record-extraction is ASSERTION-ONLY: it extracts the per-person assertions for every household member (Thomas, Bridget, Patrick, John) — including relationship-type assertions for the children — and creates/reuses the record's S-entry, but it writes NO tree persons, names, or relationships. Minting the sibling person stubs (Bridget, John) and writing their ParentChild edges is person-evidence's household-skeleton job (via materialize_facts create-or-enrich + tree_edit add_relationship), not extraction's; `mcp__genealogy__tree_edit` is not in record-extraction's frontmatter. The mid-research-flynn scenario seeds Patrick (I1) and Thomas (I2) — plus Mary (I3) and James (I4), prior-research children documented from St. Mary's baptismal registers (R2/R3 cite S5, not this census). Mary and James do NOT appear on this 1850 census, and Bridget/John (on the census) are not yet in the tree: the record-vs-tree children discrepancy is an identity question the skill must SURFACE in its summary, never a data error to 'fix' by writing, renaming, or removing tree persons. This test discriminates (a) full atomic per-person extraction with the pre-1880 `_inferred` relationship rule, (b) surfacing the identity discrepancy, and (c) the negative guard that extraction touches no tree persons/edges even when the user asks about the siblings.

judge_context: Override for Correctness and Completeness: this suite reuses one project scenario for every record, so the record is usually about people other than the project's objective (e.g. a Becker or Ferber record in a Patrick Flynn project). That mismatch is intended and is not an error by the skill. Do not lower any score because the record concerns someone else.

The skill makes one extraction_append call with the record id and relays each record's summary verbatim. Grade that call and that relay; the classifications are decided in code and are checked by the expected_classifications validator, not by you.
